_comment: RULE 20 -- THE REPLACEMENT ECONOMY: the Axis Replacement Pool (20.66), the Axis Truck Production Chart (20.66a), the Commonwealth Infantry Production Table (20.78B), and the Commonwealth Production Chart (20.78C). Transcribed cell-by-cell from the scan (tmp/The Campaign for North Africa.pdf) per scratchpad/port/transcriptions/20.66-axis-replacements-and-20.62-charge.md (PDF p.176 + rule text p.032), 20.78B-cw-infantry-replacements.md (PDF p.141 + p.031/032), and 20.78C-cw-tank-gun-replacements.md (PDF p.141 + p.032/088). Each was read at 300dpi and adversarially verified. This file is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the per-point tonnage that data/logistics_rates.json:equivalent_weights_54_5.replacement_point_tons forward-references. Block 7.2a (game/replacements.py + game/engine._replacement_production) reads it to model THE FLOW IN -- the Commonwealth infantry random stream, and the availability/lead-time/tonnage of the draw-at-will pools; Block 7.2b will build THE SPEND (a unit absorbing a Replacement Point via the already-wired UNIT_REBUILT path).

arrival_lead_time._comment: How long between PLANNING a Replacement Point (its chart Date/Dates column) and its ARRIVAL on the map. OWNER RULING 1 (Eve, PHASE-7-OWNER-RULINGS.md): the Commonwealth lead is FOUR Game-Turns -- the [20.21]/[20.78B]-footnote value (~1 month), consistent with 20.72's own worked example; 20.72's prose 'two months' is loose. So a [20.78B/C] Date is the PLAN turn and on-map arrival = Date + 4 (the Shermans land ~GT93, not GT89). The Axis Pool keeps its own printed [20.63] TWO-Game-Turn lead.

axis_tonnage_errata_20_62._comment: NAMED ERRATA KEY (the 54.17 demolition class -- never applied silently). OWNER RULING 6 (Eve, ASSUMED): the shipping tonnage per Axis Infantry Replacement Point is 30, NOT the 35 that rule 20.62's own worked example implies. The book prints the fact three ways and two of the three agree on 30. Trivially reversible: one constant. See scratchpad/port/transcriptions/20.66-axis-replacements-and-20.62-charge.md section 5.

reading_A_rule_20_62_example.text: 10 Italian Infantry Replacement Points ... would need 350 Tons of Shipping availability.

reading_B_pool_chart_20_66.text: The Italian (and German) Production Chart Tonnage column reads 30 for Infantry (read at 4x zoom to exclude an OCR 30-vs-35 misread).

third_source_rule_56_24.text: 10 Infantry Points ... this would subtract 300 tons from the available tonnage for that Game-Turn.

axis_tonnage_errata_20_62.ruling: USE 30 tons per Axis Infantry Replacement Point (both German and Italian print 30). The chart's own Tonnage column and rule 56.24's worked example agree; only 20.62's own example says 35. Same shape as ruling 1 -- a loose prose example against a printed case value.

axis_pool_20_66._comment: [20.66] THE AXIS REPLACEMENT POOL, PDF p.176. Draw-at-will (like [20.61]): the Axis Player elects each OpStage how many of each type to bring in, bounded by (a) 'number' the campaign-total cap, (b) 'max' per period the rate cap, and (c) 'plan_gt' the first Game-Turn a type may be planned. Every point is charged 'tonnage' against the [56.5] convoy allowance (20.62) at PRIORITY over all other supplies (20.64), planned 2 Game-Turns ahead (20.63), and runs the Malta gauntlet. [20.67] 'Axis Replacement Point Type Limitations Chart' is NOT a fourth chart -- it is the max/plan_gt columns embedded here (transcription section 4). A 'plan_gt' is the FIRST Game-Turn the Max may be planned; arrival = plan_gt + 2 ([20.63]). FLAG: the per-row 'class' field is an IMPLEMENTER DERIVATION, not a transcribed column -- the scan chart has none. The tank and infantry classes are anchored (they reproduce the transcription's own enumerated totals: German 131 / Italian 204 tank points, 400 / 1200 infantry), but the recce-vs-gun split among the remaining gun/AT rows is underdetermined and awaits the deferred [20.3] Replacement Point Conversion Chart (see 'deferred'). INERT in 7.2a -- class only partitions tank vs non-tank for axis_tank_total -- but 7.2b spends it on 20.43 Training length (recce/AC/tank 6 OpStages vs gun 1), so reconcile it against [20.3]/Unit Characteristics first; see the marder3 note for the sharpest case.

german_production._key: Number = total RP of that type for the whole campaign. Max = per period below. plan_gt = first Game-Turn the point may be planned (arriving TWO Game-Turns later, 20.63). tonnage = Axis Naval Convoy tons per point (54.5 forward-references this column). max_period: 'game_turn' (bare Max), 'two_weeks' (printed '*': first-and-second / third-and-fourth week of a month), 'month' (printed 'dagger'). Note German '*' = two_weeks and dagger = month (the Italian/CW charts mark these DIFFERENTLY -- see their own keys).

items.note: ONE weapon (the 2.8cm squeeze-bore AT gun), printed as two stacked name lines with a single data row -- not two items (transcription section 3 FLAG).

items.note: class 'recce' is an IMPLEMENTER DERIVATION (the chart has no class column; [20.3], deferred, is the arbiter) and the sharpest unresolved recce-vs-gun call: the Marder III is an SP anti-tank gun (Panzerjager), yet this chart's other SP mounts are classed 'gun' (sp_105), as is the Italian semovente_75_18 and the towed version of this very weapon (pak_r_762). INERT in 7.2a -- Marder is non-tank under either class, so axis_tank_total stays 131 -- but RECONCILE against [20.3]/Unit Characteristics before 7.2b spends class on 20.43 training length (recce 6 OpStages vs gun 1).

italian_production._key: Same columns as the German chart, BUT the markers differ per this chart's own key: '*' is an ID note ('all are Autobelinda 41s, ID Code vv') NOT a cap-period, and dagger = per month. Items with two printed Number sub-rows carry a 'tiers' array (each a printed sub-row {number, max, max_period, plan_first, plan_last}); the item 'number' is the campaign total = sum of the tier numbers. Per the key, the FIRST Number is the cap DURING its window and the second becomes available later. 'Note that only two points of each type may be called up during a game-turn.' tonnage is a per-item constant. The tri-nation French rows (marked double-dagger) sit in the Tunis box (plan_gt 39, no two-week delay, land/coastal-shippable).

tiers.note: this 100-point pool spans GT5-24 (the key: '...the maximum of 100 infantry replacement points may be planned during game-turns 5 through 24'); this sub-row is its GT5-8 rate.
printed Number is '--' (dash): NO new pool, only the higher GT9-24 rate on the SAME 100 as the tier above. number 0 keeps the tier-sum == item number invariant.

truck_production_20_66a._key: [20.66a] AXIS TRUCK PRODUCTION CHART. Trucks are the binding constraint of the whole campaign (53.0; scratchpad/port/faucet-audit.md) and this is a faucet into the last mile. Each Truck Type prints ONE Number and Tonnage but TWO Max/Dates tiers -- a low per-Game-Turn cap for the early window and a higher one from GT13. 'number' = total Truck Points of that type for the campaign; tiers[].max = per game-turn; tiers[].first_gt = first Game-Turn that Max may be PLANNED (arriving two weeks / 2 Game-Turns later). tonnage = Axis Naval Convoy tons per Truck Point.

commonwealth_infantry_production_20_78B._comment: [20.78B] COMMONWEALTH INFANTRY PRODUCTION TABLE, PDF p.141. A RANDOM PRODUCTION STREAM, not a fixed schedule: ONE 2d6 roll EVERY Game-Turn (20.73 'the Player uses a random dice roll to determine what Infantry ... Points he receives per turn'), looked up against whichever GT-range column contains the PLAN turn. Production runs GT3 through GT107 inclusive (105 rolls); GT1-2 and GT108-111 fall outside all four columns and produce none. Arrives FOUR Game-Turns later (arrival_lead_time.commonwealth_game_turns), always at Cairo or Alexandria (20.76), one city for a Game-Turn's whole batch (20.78B footnote), FREE of any shipping/tonnage cost (20.75). Unmodified in BOTH campaign start points ([64.54.B] 'No change'). Expected campaign yield = 1615.89 Infantry Replacement Points (game.replacements.cw_infantry_expected_yield), matching the port plan's '~1,617'. GT107 + the 4-GT lead = GT111 exactly, so the last productive roll lands its RP on the last Game-Turn (transcription section 6). 'none' cells are 0.

commonwealth_production_20_78C._comment: [20.78C] COMMONWEALTH PRODUCTION CHART, PDF p.141 -- the CW tank/gun/AA Replacement-Point schedule. Draw-at-will, Axis-Pool style, NO die roll (20.73 carves Infantry/Trucks OUT of this; everything here is elected). FREE -- no tonnage, no shipping, no interdiction (20.75); this is the Commonwealth's structural late-war advantage. Bounded by 'number' (campaign total), 'max' per period, and the plan window (plan_first / plan_last). Arrives FOUR Game-Turns after the plan turn (arrival_lead_time.commonwealth_game_turns), at Cairo/Alexandria then Training (20.43). Every UNUSED point here = 1 Commonwealth Victory Point (64.74). The 'Tiger Convoy' (GT32) is IN ADDITION to this chart. Reduced for the shorter Desert-Fox campaign by [64.54.C] (see shorter_campaign_reductions_64_54C).
commonwealth_production_20_78C._key: number (#) = campaign-total cap. max = per period. max_period: 'game_turn' (bare), 'month' (printed '*'), 'two_weeks' (printed dagger) -- NOTE these markers are the REVERSE of the German chart (transcription section 1). plan_first / plan_last = the window (in Game-Turns) the point may be PLANNED; a single printed Date has plan_last=null (runs to campaign end). class drives 20.43 Training length (gun=1 OpStage, tank/ac/recce=6).

items.name: Sherman
items.note: The decisive late-war medium: 62 RP, Max 12 per Game-Turn (no per-month marker), first plan-GT 89, no cutoff, free to ship. On-map arrival = 89 + 4 = GT93 (ruling 1).

items.name: Churchill
items.note: Max printed as '-' (dash): only 1 exists, no rate cap is meaningful.

shorter_campaign_reductions_64_54C._comment: [64.54.C] For the SHORTER (Desert-Fox-start, GT26-111) campaign these nine items are REDUCED TO (not by) the numbers below; every other row is unaffected. The full GT1-111 campaign uses 'items' above unchanged ([64.54] A/B: Truck and Infantry tables 'No change'). Applied only when the scenario runs the shorter start.

replacement_conversion_20_3._comment: [20.3] REPLACEMENT POINT CONVERSION CHART (Block 7.2b). What one Replacement TOE Strength Point of a given unit TYPE costs in Replacement Points of a given CLASS. This is the bridge between the flow-in pools (keyed by class -- infantry / tank / artillery / anti_tank / anti_air / armr) and THE SPEND: a depleted unit is rebuilt by drawing its type's cost from the co-classed pool (19.61/19.64/20.4). Rows with an empty `requires` cost NOTHING (the Road/Railroad Construction battalions rebuild free, note f). `requires` is a list of ALTERNATIVES (OR); each alternative is a list of {class,count} requirements (AND, e.g. Heavy Weapons = 1 Infantry AND 1 Gun).
replacement_conversion_20_3._source: PDF p.102, rendered at 300dpi and read with eyes (scan-verified 2026-07-24). The docs/rules/90-charts:1059-1163 OCR is SCRAMBLED for rows 12-14 -- it shifts the Armored Reconnaissance / Armored Car / Tank costs up one row (giving 'Armored Car -> 1 Tank', 'Tank -> 1 Artillery') -- and is NOT trusted. The scan is the arbiter: Armored Reconnaissance -> 1 ArmR or 1 Lt Tank; Armored Car -> 2 ArmR or 1 Lt Tank; Tank -> 1 Tank.

_key.Gun: Artillery, anti-tank or anti-air, whatever its ratings.
_key.ArmR: Armored Reconnaissance/Armored Car. Italian ArmR replacement points are always treated as Autobelinda 41's (ID Code 'vv'), even if not able to upgrade the unit under Case 20.5.
_key.Lt Tank: Light Tank of the type specified in Case 20.5. This only applies if upgrading the unit.
_key.Lt AT: Only Italian 47/32 or German 2.8cm or 28/20 Pak anti-tank guns.

rows.name: Motorcycle Reconnaissance, Camel Cavalry or Reconnaissance

notes.a: Specifically the Layforce or Special Air Service Brigade.
notes.b: Specifically units of the Italian 185th Folgore or German Ramcke Brigade.
notes.c: Whether or not it bears a motorized symbol.
notes.d: All units except those of the Ramcke Brigade.
notes.f: Specifically the Commonwealth Player's one South African Road Construction Battalion and two New Zealand Railroad Construction Battalions. If eliminated, the unit is returned to play as a reinforcement during the sixth Operations Stage after the Operations Stage in which the unit was eliminated.
notes.g: Only applies if assigning anti-tank TOE Strength Points to headquarters of the 185th Folgore Division and/or the headquarters of the Ramcke Brigade.

training_chart_17_6._comment: [17.6] TRAINING CHART -- the number of Operations Stages an arrived Replacement Point of each type must Train (rule 20.43) before a depleted unit may absorb it. 3 Operations Stages = 1 Game-Turn (rule 5.1). The chart's footnote: 'the # is the number of Operations Stages needed to train that type of Replacement Point or raise any type of an untrained Commonwealth unit's Basic Morale one point. The Commando Replacement Point must be trained by its assigned unit. Note that the time required for training guns is more of an uncrating cost than training necessity.' 20.43's OWN inline table (Gun 1 / Infantry 3 / Tank,AC,Recce 6) agrees on every row it shares; [17.6] is the formal chart it points to and adds the Commando (12) and Commonwealth-Unit (6) rows.
training_chart_17_6._scan: PDF p.100, rendered at 300dpi and read cell-by-cell (scratchpad/port/transcriptions/17.3-20.43-training.md section 4; matches docs/rules/90-charts-tables-and-play-aids.md OCR lines 875-885 verbatim). Chart rows: 'Infantry (except Commando)' 3, 'Tank or Recce' 6, 'Gun' 1, 'Commando' 12, 'Commonwealth Unit' 6. No 54.17-class OCR error here -- every cell crisp.
training_chart_17_6._key: opstages = Operations Stages of Training, keyed by the Replacement-Point TYPE (the pool 'type' field). 'ac' (armored car) is 6 by 20.43's inline 'Tank, AC, Recce Replacement -- Six' grouping (the [17.6] chart's 'Tank or Recce' row does not name AC separately). 'commonwealth_unit' (6) is the SEPARATE 17.3 UNIT-morale track (raise an untrained CW unit's Basic Morale one point per 6 Operations Stages, rule 17.34) -- transcribed here for chart completeness, but its consumer (the morale climb) is DEFERRED: the per-unit Untrained Basic Morale values live on the OA Sheets, NOT in this rulebook scan (transcription section 7). Only the RP-training DELAY reads this chart today (game.replacements.training_opstages / training_delay_gt), and only the CW-infantry producer is wired, so only the 'infantry' row (3 -> a 1-Game-Turn delay) bites live.

victory_replacement_points_64_74._comment: [64.74] REPLACEMENT VICTORY POINTS (Block 7.3, game.campaign_victory.decide). At game end each Player scores ONE Victory Point per UNUSED Replacement Point allotted in his Production Charts -- unused = the campaign-total 'number' (this file's charts) MINUS the Replacement Points THE SPEND has drawn from the pool (summed from the UNIT_REBUILT event log). Scored only in the point-tally path (64.73 opener 'failing the above two cases'), and only when the scenario runs the rule-20 economy (GameState.replacement_production); a scenario with no Production system has no allotted Replacement Points and scores none.
victory_replacement_points_64_74._scan: PDF p.088, read on the render with eyes 2026-07-24 (scratchpad/port/transcriptions/20.78C-cw-tank-gun-replacements.md section 5, and the docs/rules OCR at 64-...:81 agree verbatim): 'Each Player receives one point for each unused Replacement Point allotted to him in his Production Charts, NOT INCLUDING PLANES AND/OR TRUCKS AND, FOR THE COMMONWEALTH PLAYER ONLY, INFANTRY. Thus, if the Commonwealth Player had a total of 35 Crusader I Tank Replacement Points available for the game, but he uses only 18, he gains 17 points.' The worked example (35 - 18 = 17) cross-checks: 35 is exactly the [20.78C] Crusader Mk I 'number'.

excluded_classes._comment: [64.74] PERMANENT exclusions, verbatim from the printed rule (see _scan): planes and Trucks for BOTH sides, and Infantry FOR THE COMMONWEALTH ONLY -- Axis infantry Replacement Points DO score under the book. 'plane'/'truck' name classes absent from the charts this file scores (air is a separate establishment; the [20.66a]/[20.78A] truck streams are separate), so they filter nothing live; only the Commonwealth 'infantry' entry bites. This set is now BOOK-FAITHFUL: the earlier interim proxy that ALSO dropped Axis infantry was REVERTED 2026-07-24 when Eve ruled 64.74 scores only SPENDABLE classes (see spendable_classes) -- the spendable gate, not an exclusion, is what keeps unbuilt-spend Axis infantry from scoring, so no deviation from the scan remains here.

spendable_classes._comment: OWNER RULING 2026-07-24 (Eve): 64.74 scores UNUSED Replacement Points only for classes the engine can currently SPEND. Rationale -- 'unused' presupposes 'usable'; a class with no rebuild beat is 100% unused by construction, which is not husbandry (what 64.74 rewards) but an unmodelled spend, and scoring it produced a fixed Axis+893 / CW+958 constant that compressed every campaign grade toward 1:1 (the Gate 7A artifact). Today the ONLY live spend is the Commonwealth infantry rebuild (engine._replacement_spend, pool_key ALLIED/infantry) -- which is ALSO book-excluded, so 64.74 correctly scores 0/0 until a non-infantry spend lands. GROWS ONE EDIT AT A TIME: when the [20.78C] Commonwealth equipment spend lands add its classes to ALLIED (tank/gun score -- CW armour is not excluded); when the [20.66] Axis spend + [20.62] coupling lands add AXIS (infantry/tank/gun score -- only CW infantry is excluded). The used-subtraction then bites for real. This carries the engine-state truth the reverted proxy used to smuggle into excluded_classes.
